newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses mixed in thin pre-Xmas trade.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses mixed in thin pre-Xmas trade.

text.p: European bourses began the day mixed in thin trading on Monday ahead of the Christmas break with some investors taking profits after recent strong gains.
On currency markets, the dollar was barely changed from levels seen late on Friday and business was quiet with most dealing rooms winding down for the holiday.

London's FTSE index just about struggled into the plus column in early trading after closing at a record on Friday as most European bourses were swept higher in a Christmas buying spree on Wall Street.
"We saw a good performance on Friday. The market has a good undertone to it. This is not the time of year when institutions want to let go of shares," said one dealer.
The FTSE blue chip index slipped in and out of profit but was showing a gain of 4.3 points by mid-morning. The index closed at a peak of 4,077.6 on Friday, eclipsing the record set on October 21.
Stocks had climbed as high as 4,100 on Friday, carried by a dramatic two percent jump on Wall Street the day before, but eased back as New York's rally ran out of steam later on Friday.

No British figures were due on Monday but traders were keeping an eye open for the U.S. November personal income and spending data to be released at 1330 GMT. A U.S. survey on consumer confidence for November was due at 1500 GMT.
Frankfurt's DAX index climbed 1.66 percent on Friday, was down 0.4 percent and the thin trading was likely to preclude any chance of a revival of the pre-Christmas rally.
"We will be lucky if all the DAX shares have started trading by the floor opening," said one Frankfurt dealer, referring to the sluggish start electronic dealings.
In Paris, shares slipped a few points on the last day of the December account with many investors taking profits.
Moulinex was down 3.69 percent at 117.50. The company on Friday announced it had cut its first half loss and announced plans for a 500 million franc ($95 million) capital increase.
On the currency front, the dollar was at 1.5537 marks and 114.16 yen, compared to 1.5521 and 114.20 in late European trade on Friday.
Traders will be awaiting the U.S. economic data due later, which will give clues on the health of the American economy, but were thought unlikely to have an immediate implications for interest rates.
Although the most likely scenario was for the dollar to remain at current levels in narrow ranges, any sharp moves on U.S. asset markets would have a knock-on effect, dealers said.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5537 marks and 114.16 yen, compared with 1.5521 marks and 114.20 yen in late European business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 3.8 points, at 4,081.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 2.72 at 2,275.46.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 11.13 points at 2,843.32.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $368.70 an ounce, compared to $369.35 on Friday. Silver was unhanged at $4.84.
